h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ז׳ Pesach — Maamar Zayin

p: לְפִיכָךְ אֲנַחְנוּ חַיָּיבִים לְהוֹדוֹת וְכוּלֵּי... לְמִי שֶׁעָשָׂה לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ וְלָנוּ וְכוּלֵּי.
"Therefore we are obligated to thank, etc.... to Him Who (l'Mi she'asah) performed for our forefathers and for us, etc."
בַּגְּמָרָא
In the Gemara
(בְּרָכוֹת נ'.):
(Berachos 50a):
לְמִי שֶׁאָכַלְנוּ — הֲרֵי זֶה בּוּר וְכוּלֵּי;
"[One who says] 'to Him of Whom we have eaten' is an ignorant boor, etc.;
וְהָא אָמְרִינַן: לְמִי שֶׁעָשָׂה לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ וְכוּלֵּי?
but do we not say 'to Him Who performed for our forefathers, etc.'?
אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם מוּכְחָא מִילְּתָא.
He said to him: There the matter is self-evident."
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים קָשֶׁה: לָמָּה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר "לְמִי"?
Still, there is a difficulty: why did he need to say "to Mi (Whom)"?
הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר "לַה'" אוֹ "לֵאלֹהֵינוּ"!
He should have said "to Hashem" or "to our God"!
אַךְ "מִי" הַיְינוּ בִּינָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
However, "Mi" refers to Binah, as brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' קט"ו:),
וְכָאן תֵּשַׁע לְשׁוֹנוֹת: לְהוֹדוֹת, לְהַלֵּל, לְשַׁבֵּחַ, לְפָאֵר, לְרוֹמֵם, לְהַדֵּר, לְבָרֵךְ, לְעַלֶּה, וּלְקַלֵּס,
and here there are nine expressions—to thank, to praise, to laud, to glorify, to exalt, to adorn, to bless, to elevate, and to acclaim
וּ"לְמִי" לָשׁוֹן עֲשִׂירִי: מִי — בִּינָה
and "l'Mi" is the tenth expression: Mi is Binah
(עַיֵּין תּוֹסְפוֹת יוֹם טוֹב פְּסָחִים י', ה').
(see Tosafos Yom Tov, Pesachim 10:5).
וְחָשַׁב: הוֹצִיאָנוּ מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵירוּת — עָלְמָא דְּחֵירוּ, בִּינָה,
And it enumerated: "He brought us out from slavery to freedom"—the World of Freedom, Binah,
וִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם מִסִּטְרָא דְּיוֹבֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
for the Exodus from Egypt came from the aspect of Yovel (Jubilee/Binah), as brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' קכ"ה.)
עַל הַפָּסוּק
on the verse
(שְׁמוֹת י"ג, י"ח):
(Shemos 13:18):
וַחֲמֻשִׁים עָלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל;
"And armed/fifty-fold (chamushim) the Children of Israel went up";
וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁלֹשׁ לְשׁוֹנוֹת: מִיָּגוֹן לְשִׂמְחָה, מֵאֵבֶל לְיוֹם טוֹב, וּמֵאֲפֵילָה לְאוֹר גָּדוֹל — כְּנֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת;
and afterward three expressions—"from sorrow to joy, from mourning to a festive day, and from deep darkness to great light"—corresponding to the first three Sefiros;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִשִּׁיעְבּוּד לִגְאוּלָּה כָּאָמוּר.
and afterward "from subjugation to redemption," as stated.
וְחָמֵשׁ הַלְּשׁוֹנוֹת כְּנֶגֶד חָמֵשׁ מַדְרֵיגוֹת שֶׁבַּנֶּפֶשׁ: נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה, חַיָּה, יְחִידָה
And the five expressions correspond to the five levels of the soul: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah
(דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ב', ל"ו),
(Devarim Rabbah 2:36),
וְהֵם כְּנֶגֶד אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת הֲוָיָ"ה וְקוֹצוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְכֶתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
and they correspond to the four letters of Havayah and the upper tip of the Yud, which alludes to Kesser Elyon
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' ס"ה:):
(Zohar, Vol. 3, 65b):
מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵירוּת — בִּינָה, עָלְמָא דְּחֵירוּ;
"from slavery to freedom" is Binah, the World of Freedom;
מִשִּׁיעְבּוּד לִגְאוּלָּה — נֶגֶד מִדַּת מַלְכוּת;
"from subjugation to redemption" corresponds to the attribute of Malchus;
וְחָשַׁב שָׁלֹשׁ לְשׁוֹנוֹת נֶגֶד יוּ"ד וְקוֹצוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד, שֶׁמִּזֶּה בְּחִינַת חַיָּה יְחִידָה, נְשָׁמָה לִנְשָׁמָה,
and it reckoned three expressions corresponding to Yud and the tip of the Yud—from which come the aspects of Chayah and Yechidah, the soul of the soul
ו' שֶׁמִּזֶּה הָרוּחַ:
and Vav, from which comes Ruach:
לְשִׂמְחָה — יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"to joy" is the union of the Holy One, blessed is He, and Knesses Yisrael, as it is said
(תְּהִלִּים קמ"ט, ב'):
(Tehillim 149:2):
יִשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֹשָׂיו בְּנֵי צִיּוֹן יָגִילוּ בְמַלְכָּם.
"Let Israel rejoice in its Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King."
וְחָמֵשׁ הַלְּשׁוֹנוֹת וְכָל אֶחָד מֵהֶם כָּלוּל מֵעֶשֶׂר — חֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה.
And the five expressions, each one comprising ten, equal the fifty gates of Binah.
וְהָעֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ נָגוֹף לְמִצְרַיִם וְרָפוֹא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
And the ten plagues, which were "smiting for Egypt and healing for Israel,"
וַעֲלֵיהֶם אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מֵהֶם הָיָה כָּלוּל מֵחָמֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן,
concerning which Rabbi Akiva said that each one was also composed of five,
כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה כֹּחוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁהֵם מֵאַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת הֲוָיָ"ה וְקוֹצוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד, חֲמִשָּׁה פַּרְצוּפִין
corresponding to the five faculties of the soul that stem from the four letters of Havayah and the tip of the Yud, the five Partzufim
וְלָקוּ חֲמִשִּׁים מַכּוֹת.
so they were smitten with fifty plagues.
וּבִקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף אַף לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי לָקוּ חֲמִשִּׁים מַכּוֹת.
And at the Splitting of the Sea, even according to Rabbi Yosei HaGalili, they were smitten with fifty plagues.
וְהַכֹּל כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה פַּרְצוּפִין, חֲמִשָּׁה "בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי" שֶׁבַּגְּמָרָא
And all of this corresponds to the five Partzufim, the five utterances of "Bless, O my soul" in the Gemara
(בְּרָכוֹת י'.),
(Berachos 10a),
וְחָמֵשׁ מַדְרֵיגוֹת שֶׁבַּנֶּפֶשׁ, וַחֲמִשָּׁה כֹּחוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
and the five levels of the soul, and the five faculties of the soul,
וִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי שֶׁזָּכוּ לַחֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַחֲמֻשִׁים עָלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and the Exodus from Egypt occurred because they merited the fifty gates of Binah, as it is said: "And fifty-fold (chamushim) the Children of Israel went up."

paragraphs.text: Berachos 50a — "R. Yochanan said: 'Let us bless Him of Whose we have eaten' — this is a scholar; 'To Whom (le-Mi) we have eaten' — this is an ignoramus. R. Acha said to R. Ashi: But we say, 'To Him (le-Mi) Who did for our fathers and for us all these miracles'? He answered: There the matter is evident: who works miracles? The Holy One." Rashi: with miracles there is no room to mistake Whom is meant.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 115b (Mishpatim, Ra'aya Mehemna) — "[Binah] is the world of Yovel, the fifty letters of the Unification… But in the World to Come, which is the world of Yovel, where the fifty letters of Krias Shema are, no chazzan can discharge a person's obligation… and so it alludes: 'If I am not for myself, who (mi) is for me?' — Mi is surely the world of Yovel." Thus "Mi" is Binah. (Lublin 1901 reads II 115b; Rav Tzadok cites the same daf for "Mi = Binah" elsewhere.)

paragraphs.text: Tosafos Yom Tov, Pesachim 10:5 (on "to thank, to praise…") — Tosafos count seven expressions for the seven heavens; "I can uphold our reading of nine, for there are nine heavens… and with the tenth he says 'To Him Who did,' for He rides upon Aravos." Thus "le-Mi" is the tenth expression.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, First Night of Pesach 54 — “The word ‘Eleh’ denotes the spreading out of all the particulars… In exile they seem separate particulars. But when the name ‘Mi’ shines in them, one recognizes their oneness, for at the root they are in complete unity. This oneness is what the name Mi signifies: it is the fiftieth gate of the fifty gates of Binah, which unites all forty-nine gates… Therefore after the Exodus, when Israel began to refine all forty-nine attributes by their choice, they were commanded to count forty-nine days until the fiftieth, when the light of the fiftieth gate shines.” Connection: Sod Yesharim shares the reading of “Mi” as Binah and its fifty gates, and adds that Mi is specifically the fiftieth gate, the one that unifies the scattered particulars.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yosef Gikatilla, Shaarei Orah, Gate 8 (Binah) — “The two Sefiros that are Havayah and Adnus are aligned opposite each other; the upper one is called Tehillah, praise, and the lower one is called Tefillah, prayer. Therefore it is called Tehillah, meaning that we must laud and praise Him Who performed for us and for our forefathers all these miracles and brought us out from slavery to freedom. Binah is the secret of praise—to praise, laud, glorify and exalt for all the good, miracles and wonders He does with us—because it is the secret of freedom and redemption, and when it shines forth, the miracles and wonders appear for Israel.” Connection: Shaarei Orah assigns the Haggadah's very list of praises, addressed to “Him Who performed,” to Binah, and gives the reason: Binah is the source of freedom from which the miracles issue.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Chaim Chaikel of Amdur, Chaim VaChesed 250 — “It is written, ‘Return, wayward children’: these are the sparks that fell into physicality, sparks of love and fear. This is accomplished through Binah, the World of Freedom, which frees the mind: by understanding the greatness of the Creator, a person liberates his mind from physicality. This is the blessing of the new month, ‘He Who (Mi) performed miracles for our forefathers’—Mi is Binah (Zohar II 117)—through which the mind is raised out of physicality. And this is ‘from slavery to freedom’: through the greatness of the Creator that a person grasps with his own understanding.” Connection: Like Rav Tzadok, the Amdurer reads “Mi” in the formula of thanks as Binah, the World of Freedom; he adds the inner avodah, that a person's own understanding of the Creator's greatness is what brings his mind from slavery to freedom.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 125a (Nasso) — "Israel, of whom it is said, 'And the Children of Israel went up chamushim from the land of Egypt' — from the side of the Tree of Life, which are the fifty years of the Yovel; of them it is said, 'They shall go up on the mountain'…" The Exodus came from the side of the Yovel (Binah).

paragraphs.text: Berachos 10a — "These five 'Barchi nafshi' — whom did David say them about? Only about the Holy One and about the soul: just as the Holy One fills the whole world, so the soul fills the whole body…" (five parallels follow). Rashi: the five "Barchi nafshi" are those listed earlier on the page.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beshalach 5 — “The ten plagues were already ‘smiting for Egypt and healing for Israel’; in each they were refined in one attribute, leaving the kelipah and entering the corresponding attribute in holiness… Yet in the other eight attributes, though refined, the light did not shine for them even after the Exodus… These eight are contained in three letters of the Name, the source of Nefesh, Ruach and Neshamah. But in the two last attributes, from below upward, Chochmah and Kesser, the Yud and the tip of the Yud, from which come Chayah and Yechidah, the light of Torah already shone in their heart; therefore it says, ‘and chamushim the Children of Israel went up,’ the fifty gates of Binah.” Connection: The same mapping of the plagues and the five soul-levels onto Havayah and “chamushim,” adding that at the Exodus only Chayah and Yechidah were lit, and the rest only at the Sea.

— “The ten plagues were already ‘smiting for Egypt and healing for Israel’; in each they were refined in one attribute, leaving the kelipah and entering the corresponding attribute in holiness… Yet in the other eight attributes, though refined, the light did not shine for them even after the Exodus… These eight are contained in three letters of the Name, the source of Nefesh, Ruach and Neshamah. But in the two last attributes, from below upward, Chochmah and Kesser, the Yud and the tip of the Yud, from which come Chayah and Yechidah, the light of Torah already shone in their heart; therefore it says, ‘and chamushim the Children of Israel went up,’ the fifty gates of Binah.” Connection: The same mapping of the plagues and the five soul-levels onto Havayah and “chamushim,” adding that at the Exodus only Chayah and Yechidah were lit, and the rest only at the Sea.
